principle_text: When the persuadee expresses interest in charitable giving, you should affirm the moral importance of the cause and clearly highlight the specific needs the donation will address.
When the persuadee shows curiosity about a charity's purpose, you should provide clear, concise information that encourages them to ask more questions and engage deeply.
When the persuadee shows unfamiliarity with the charity, you should provide informative background highlighting its history and broad impact to engage their curiosity and interest.
When the persuadee shows unfamiliarity with a charity, you should provide specific information about its causes and highlight its efficiency to increase their interest and engagement.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or off-topic remarks, avoid making casual comments that do not steer the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows only mild interest and uncertainty about the charity, avoid admitting limited knowledge or changing topics that do not build trust or clarify the cause.
When the persuadee is uncertain about specific details of the charity, avoid asking questions that only confirm facts without linking them to the donation appeal.
When the persuadee shows only vague familiarity with a charity, avoid making uncertain comparisons that do not clearly explain the charity's value or impact.
When the persuadee acknowledges a donation request without showing commitment or hesitation, avoid making a direct ask without first building clearer agreement or motivation to donate.
When the persuadee shows curiosity about a charitable organization, you should provide clear, positive, and concise information to increase their interest and engagement.
When the persuadee shows curiosity or mild skepticism about donating, you should share your own concrete donation experience to create relatability and encourage further engagement.

When the persuadee shares limited donation activity without expressing willingness to donate, avoid only asking about their past charity involvement without guiding them toward donation opportunities.
When the persuadee expresses a focus on a particular charitable cause, you should align your message with that cause to build rapport and encourage engagement.
When the persuadee responds with vague or unrelated information, avoid introducing specific charity names without first establishing their interest or connection to those organizations.
